Even a brilliant technologist can mess up. Bill Gates was a brilliant technologist when he cofounded Microsoft , but he has never managed to completely integrate Microsoft into the world, and its share price has collapsed in response to poor results. And so the question arises: what would have happened if the company had kept Gates out of it from the start? To find out, IBM scientists in Cambridge, Massachusetts set up a computerized e-mail server in 2004, which was designed to test whether the e-mail server could be programmed to respond to an e-mail from a different user. In the end, this test succeeded. So what did the researchers do? They wrote an e-mail from Gates with a message from himself, which would never have been sent. target: modern man in the Philippines is not exactly the same as day in the life of a modern man in the United States, much less a man from the Middle East. That's not to say that globalization is bad. It is, and will continue to be, an important factor in Philippine culture, just as it’s been in the United States for centuries. But, it creates a different experience in the lives of those in the Philippines who are born and raised there. It is, in this sense, a “global” experience, one that has a more or less universal appeal. And so the Philippines began to change, and to be changed, from one generation to the next. In many ways, the development of modern Manila began before globalization itself. input: IT alligator tales I grew up in New York, where giant alligators -- sometimes more ornately described as albino alligators -- were rumored to roamIT Myth 5: Most IT projects fail Do most IT projects fail? Some point to the number of giant consultancies such as IBM Global Services, Capgemini
target: , and Accenture. IT consulting firms have made a fortune, and they attract a lot of criticism. But the facts don't match myth The big problem with IT is that it is often difficult to measure success. For IT, it is the cost of the services that matters. That can lead to very poor projects with high project costs. IT is also very large. According to a recent study by the McKinsey Institute, more than 60% of the IT organization has more than 100,000 employees. A survey by IBM found that more than half of those IT organizations have more than 500 employees, with many more people in operations and infrastructure. IT is expensive, and it's hard to measure success. The largest IT consulting firms, including those cited above, do have success stories. But they are not as successful as companies such as IBM. IBM spends around $6 billion on consulting services per year. That seems like a lot of money. However, the consulting firm's clients are relatively small.

target:
red object in the night sky, I asked my husband what he thought.

The answer? "I don't know what the hell that is." I have never heard anyone describe Venus as red.

It is actually a brilliant blue-black star, with a red light emitted by its atmosphere. It's not really known how the planet Venus is seen to vary in brightness with its passage in and out of the Sun over a series of months. Venus has not orbited the Sun in the past 12,000 years, so we have no records. And it's only in the past few hundred years or so that scientists became interested in Venus' proximity to the Sun, and started studying its atmosphere with spacecraft like the European Space Agency's Venus Express and NASA's Venus Express and Pioneer Venus Express missions.

But Venus has changed since the early days of human exploration of the Solar System. During the 1970s, when Venus was first discovered, the planet's atmosphere was relatively thick.

input: Italy's Pennetta Wins Idea Prokom Open (AP) AP - Italy's Flavia Pennetta won the Idea Prokom Open for her first WTough Race Ahead for Swimmer Phelps  ATHENS (Reuters) - Michael Phelps, his first gold medal  safely gathered in, eased through the next
target: stage of his Olympic career with a time more than a second faster than the second place finisher in the 100 meters butterfly on Saturday. The gold was Phelps' sixth and his first medal at the Games, his fifth in a row  and gave him a total of nine golds, eight silvers and two bronze medals since swimming's debut at the 1900 Paris Games. It also was Phelps' second gold medal in the event in the past three Olympics, after winning it in 2004. The 24-year-old, who is now the most decorated Olympian in history with six golds and eight medals overall, finished in 51.61. He was one hundredth of a second faster than the second place finisher in the 100 butterfly.  Phelps was in his fifth Olympics, his first since 2008 and his first outside the United States. He was also competing at his sixth Olympics. His performance Saturday was more than a second better than the first place finisher in the 100 fly this year.

That compares with $4.8 billion for executive salaries and $5.8 billion for executive bonuses a year earlier, and represents little change from the previous survey.
The Washington area's top compensation, including bonuses, rose by nearly 7 percent in dollar terms from a year ago, when it fell in real terms, the survey showed, while salary and bonuses fell by nearly 8 percent in real terms.
"We saw a year with fewer executive bonuses, and pay rises for those that were given," said Joe Dawson, director of research and consultancy services for Thomson Reuters/Freelance.
"Companies were more willing to give them and companies were rewarding them for growth than they have been in the past."

WASHINGTON — Spending at the Pentagon rose 5.4 percent last year, up from 4.3 percent the previous year, as military programs were boosted by a $1 trillion increase in Defense Department outlays.

The Pentagon’s spending grew to $612.8 billion, according to data from the Pentagon released Thursday. And while that’s the highest yearly total on record, the annual growth rate was significantly slower than in past years.

In fact, the spending growth rate was the slowest of the decade. Spending rose 3.9 percent between 2007 and 2009, for example.

The spending increase came from the Pentagon’s massive $1 trillion increase in defense outlays, which grew to $612.8 billion.
